steps.title: What happened
items: UPV was 1.72M, down 9% WoW from the prior week’s 1.88M peak — but +20% above forecast and above the ~1.65M 4-week average.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: Terms & Conditions / SMS spike. Base customers were routed to the T&C update page (~168K visits, ~9% of UPV; ~80% via SMS), inflating UPV. These are largely authenticated base users, not net-new prospects.

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: Not materially. UPV Buy Flow held flat at 0.77M and unassisted orders were flat — the T&C traffic wasn’t converting.
Quarter outlook: even excluding the data issue, UPV was pacing ahead of forecast.

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: Unresolved data issue. Authenticated users aren’t being flagged, overcounting UPV whenever we run campaigns to existing customers.

steps.title: What happened
items: UPV came in at 1.54M this week, +6% above the 1.46M forecast (~82K visits above plan), while down 10% WoW from last week’s 1.72M.
The WoW decline is expected and healthy: the Terms & Conditions / SMS traffic that inflated the prior two weeks has fallen off — no more UPV to the T&C page.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: Primary driver — Freedom Explorer. The new $0-down financing campaign launched last week. The $0 switch page is the 3rd-largest prospect entry page this week (~83K prospects) — which almost perfectly accounts for the amount we’re running above forecast — driven mainly by paid search.
Secondary — Samsung. Still seeing activity to the Samsung page, though a little lower than last week.

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: Yes — this is healthy, prospect-driven demand. Unlike the base-user T&C spike, this volume is converting: unassisted postpaid orders are up nearly 20% WoW, also driven by Freedom Explorer.
Quarter outlook: UPV is pacing +8% ahead of forecast QTD (52% vs 48% expected at week 7), and the above-forecast volume is now coming from genuine prospect demand rather than a data artifact.

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: Lean into Freedom Explorer. Given the ~20% lift in unassisted postpaid orders, keep supporting the $0-down launch and watch the $0 switch page as a top prospect entry point.

steps.title: What happened
items: UPV came in at 1.48M, +3% above the 1.44M forecast, but down 4% WoW from 1.54M.
A softer week overall — this is backed up by store traffic being down WoW — but even so, we’re holding slightly ahead of forecast.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: Freedom Explorer is carrying the week. The $0-down page (Freedom Explorer) is now the #2 top entry page (just behind the homepage), and orders are starting from that entry point.
Paid search pulled back. The “Get Started” page declined as prospects route to the Freedom Explorer page instead, and paid search spend is down 12% WoW (paid-search UPV −9%).
Samsung held flat WoW.

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: Muted but healthy. Orders are flat WoW and UPV Flow eased to 0.74M (−4%). The softness is the expected pre-NPI lull, and we’re doing better than expected on the $0 promo — still slightly above forecast.
Quarter outlook: UPV is pacing +7% ahead of forecast QTD (59% vs 55% expected at week 8).

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: Keep leaning on Freedom Explorer. The $0 page is now a top-2 entry point and converting — it’s cushioning the paid-search pullback.

Alignment and timing of campaigns and budgets. Paid search is in its second week of lower spend (down 12% WoW). This decline happened during the Freedom Explorer launch and may limit the campaign’s effectiveness. The strategic question: should budget increase alongside aggressive offers, or be used to offset slower periods with no major offers?
Pre-NPI lull expected to persist near-term.

steps.title: What happened
items: UPV was 1.44M — just under forecast and down 3% WoW; orders 23.0K (−4%).
Some of this is the usual pre-NPI lull, but budget cuts are the bigger factor this week.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: Budget cuts are the main driver. Paid search spend has fallen four weeks straight — $7.68M → $7.17M → $6.52M → $5.45M (~29% since early August), with paid social down too. Paid-search UPV is −17% WoW (paid social −21%).
Organic is picking up some of the slack. Organic search is +4% WoW, but not enough to fully offset; other channels are flat.
Freedom Explorer felt the pullback. With less search & social funding, it slipped from the #2 to #3 entry page (−30K UPV). Back-to-school lifted the “Project 10M” page.

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: Yes — it’s reaching orders. Paid-search orders are down; organic is up but not enough to offset (orders −4%).
Quarter outlook: UPV is still +7% ahead of forecast for the quarter, but expect another step down as the remaining cuts land.

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: More paid search cuts coming. Paid search is being cut ~$4.2M this quarter; about $2.2M is already done ($7.68M → $5.45M), with the remaining cuts landing over the next two weeks — timed to avoid impacting the NPI launch.

Sharper decline than expected. Accounts are already down ~4K (VR & unassisted) — near the −5K estimated for the full paid search cut, but we’re only about halfway through it. At this rate, the impact is likely to overshoot the estimate.

steps.title: What happened
items: UPV was 1.42M — just under forecast and down 1% WoW. A quiet week: orders up 3% WoW, VR calls & chats down slightly, store traffic flat.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: Budget cuts continue. Paid search is down again (−6% WoW), with organic search picking up some of it (+4% WoW).
Freedom Explorer held #3 among entry pages but eased ~7%, in line with lower overall traffic.

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: Not much this week — roughly on forecast. UPV Flow softened, weighted more to HSI (−6%) than postpaid (−4%).
Quarter outlook: UPV is still +6% ahead of forecast for the quarter, with more paid search cuts still to land.

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: Paid search cuts pausing for NPI. Rather than cutting further, budget is being restored for the iPhone launch next week; organic had been offsetting part of the earlier decline.

steps.title: What happened
items: UPV jumped to 1.71M — up 20% WoW on the NPI ramp, but ~7% under the 1.84M forecast. Buy Flow surged to 0.97M (+41%), add-to-cart +19%, calls & chats up.
And we did it on far less spend: biddable came in ~35% under forecast vs UPV’s ~7% — strong efficiency.
Orders were down 7.5% WoW — expected, since customers couldn’t order the new iPhones yet.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: The new iPhone launch drove the surge. Interest spanned both the iPhone 18 (preorder opened Sep 12, launches Sep 18) and the new iPhone duo — the Apple iPhone Deals page broke into the top-5 entry pages, with other top pages up too.
Paid search led it (+50%+), with budget back up ($5.1M → $5.66M) — a reversal of the recent cuts for the launch.
Orders dipped because ordering wasn’t open — preorder only started Saturday (iPhone duo preorder isn’t until Oct 16).

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: Yes — the traffic that came was high-intent. UPV landed under the optimistic NPI forecast, but Buy Flow jumped +41% (add-to-cart +19%) — visitors actually dug into the phones and showed real interest, not just surface browsing.
Quarter outlook: UPV is +4% ahead of forecast for the quarter.

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: Order week is the real test. With preorder now open, watch whether this week’s traffic and cart activity convert to orders.

steps.title: What happened
items: UPV hit 1.88M — a new NPI peak, +2% above forecast and +10% WoW. Buy Flow 1.11M (+14%), add-to-cart +22% (after +19% the week before).
Web viewing peaked even as store/exit traffic fell (3.1M) — customers shifting online for the launch.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: iPhone order week — the NPI peak. Paid search was the biggest UPV driver (+19%).
Biddable spend ticked up ~13% WoW to $10.95M — still well under the ramped September forecast.

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: Yes — very high intent. Flow +14% and add-to-cart +22% show strong engagement.

Orders fell 22K → 18K, but new accounts from QGP rose 15K → 20K — so the dip likely isn’t real. Preorders may not count as activations until devices ship (Sep 18), and there may also be an Adobe tracking gap. Either way, the interest is clearly there.
Quarter outlook: UPV is +4% ahead of forecast for the quarter.

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: New EDL should sharpen order tracking. The gap between QGP accounts and Adobe orders looks like a tracking issue — and the new EDL should give us better visibility to understand and reconcile it going forward.

steps.title: What happened
items: UPV held at 1.87M — +4% above forecast and roughly flat WoW, sustaining the NPI peak. The slight softness came from search & other channels. Buy Flow eased to 0.98M (−12%) off last week’s high.
Add-to-cart eased 5% WoW off the launch-week high, while store traffic rose 10% — a shift toward in-store now that devices are available.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: NPI demand is holding, and HSI is the bright spot. HSI flow +32% while postpaid eased (−13%).
Orders rose WoW, led by HSI (unassisted +11%, assisted +5%) and paid search.

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: Yes — a strong close. We’re sustaining high UPV post-launch with an HSI boost, and orders turned back up — consistent with last week’s dip being timing, not a real drop.
Quarter outlook: UPV is pacing +4% ahead of forecast with just the final few days of Q3 left.

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: Lean into HSI momentum. The lift in HSI flow and orders is the bright spot as NPI demand sustains — worth supporting into next quarter.

steps.title: What happened
items: Q3 closed strong. The final four days (Sep 27–30) drew 0.96M visitors vs a 0.84M forecast (+14%), and orders were 9.8K (~2.5K a day).
Q4 opened (Oct 1–3) at 0.72M vs a 0.76M forecast — slightly under, but half weeks are hard to predict.
Across the full week, UPV was 1.68M — ~5% above forecast and down 10% WoW.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: Paid search kept driving most of the traffic through quarter end.
Searches for iPhone deals dropped post-launch, while HSI moved up in the entry-page rankings (HSI EC +7%, even with lower spend).
Spend dropped. Biddable spend was down 16% WoW (clicks −21%) — social fell 30% after last week’s Apple launch placements, and search was down 5%.

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: A steady close — nothing unusual. The half-week swings are normal noise, and the full week landed above forecast.
Q3 final: UPV closed at ~21.2M, +4% ahead of the 20.3M forecast.

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: Post-NPI dip ahead. Expect next week to ease to ~1.6M as launch demand fades, then pick back up once iPhone duo preorders open (Oct 16).

steps.title: What happened
items: UPV was 1.61M — right on forecast and down 4% WoW, the expected post-NPI drop-off.
Buy Flow eased to 0.85M (−6%), and orders were down 19% WoW.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: Paid search drove most of the UPV drop — the regular post-NPI fall-off, as the forecast anticipated.
Most of the Buy Flow drop came from postpaid and BYOD; HSI was down just 1%.

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: Expected — this is the normal post-NPI drop-off. It’s what the UPV forecast predicted, and HSI is holding up.
Quarter outlook: Q4 UPV is tracking close to forecast (~2% under after two weeks, all from the short first week).

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: Watch the iPhone duo pickup. The post-NPI dip landed as forecast; next up is iPhone duo preorders on Oct 16.

steps.title: What happened
items: UPV was 1.86M — +13% above forecast and up 16% WoW.
However, Buy Flow barely moved (0.87M, up from 0.85M), so many of the extra visitors didn’t enter the buying flow.
Orders fell 11% WoW (15.2K → 13.5K), mostly postpaid.

steps.title: Why it happened
items: Friday Night Lights drove a big bump, with about 110K extra visitors.
The T-Fiber address check page also jumped as an entry page, at about 85K UPV.
iPhone duo hasn’t caused a big increase yet. Possible reasons: shipping isn’t until late December, so there’s no rush to preorder, plus the normal fade after the iPhone 18 launch.

steps.title: Is it meaningful?
items: Mixed — strong traffic, softer conversion. Visitors beat forecast, but flat Buy Flow and lower orders suggest the extra traffic wasn’t high-intent.
Digital outperformed. Store traffic was flat WoW, which usually signals a solid week, so digital did better than the market.
Quarter outlook: Q4 UPV is pacing +5% ahead of forecast through three weeks.

steps.title: Recommendations & risks to watch
items: Watch iPhone duo demand. Preorders opened Oct 16 but orders are muted, with shipping not until late December. Track whether they build as the ship date nears.
